description:
FILED s464ay (Opus, round 22 review) while restoring perl-tests/sort.t's inline
`ok(1,'SKIP')` rows (task #965).  PRE-EXISTING and SILENT.

THE DISCRIMINATING REPRO (scratch/p22-sort-overload-disagree.pl) -- an overload
whose `cmp` DISAGREES with its `""`, which is the only shape that makes the bug
visible:

    package OV;
    use overload 'cmp' => sub { $_[1]{val} <=> $_[0]{val} },   # DESCENDING
                 '""'  => sub { $_[0]{val} };
    package main;
    my @o = map { bless { val => $_ }, 'OV' } (1, 2, 3);
    print "default: [@{[ sort @o ]}]\n";
    print "explicit: [@{[ sort { $a cmp $b } @o ]}]\n";

  perl 5.40.3:  default: [3 2 1]   explicit: [3 2 1]
  PCL:          default: [1 2 3]   explicit: [3 2 1]

So the `cmp` overload IS reachable (the explicit block is right, and a bare
`$x cmp $y` is right -- probed); what is wrong is sort's DEFAULT comparator,
which compares the STRINGIFICATIONS.

THE CALL COUNTS SAY THE SAME THING (scratch/p21-sort-overload.pl, two objects):
perl calls `cmp` once and `""` twice; PCL calls `cmp` ZERO times and `""` FOUR
times.  With a `cmp` that agrees with `""` the answer comes out right by
accident, which is why this never showed up as a wrong sort order in the
corpus -- it needs a class whose ordering is not its string order.

WHICH ROWS IT OWNS: perl-tests/sort.t 162 'overload compare called once',
163 'overload sort result', 164 'overload string called twice' (upstream
RT34604).  Those three ALSO need `tie %h` (#155), so they will not go green
on this fix alone -- the standalone probe above is the acceptance test.  The
same three rows exist in the companion t/op/sort.t inside its blessed count.

THE WRONG DIAGNOSIS IT HID BEHIND: the inline skip said "sort doesn't use
overloaded 'cmp' in PCL" / "sort ignores overloaded '\"\"'".  The first half
is right for the default path and the second half is backwards -- sort uses
`""` and nothing else.  Registered as three manufactured passes since the
edit, so sort.t was reported FULLY PASSING with these inside it.

FIX SHAPE (untried): sort's default comparator is the `cmp` op by definition
(perldoc -f sort: "sorts in standard string comparison order"), so it should
lower to / call the same overload-aware path `p-cmp` already uses for the
explicit block rather than a raw string compare.  Check whether the default
path is a Kind-A fast emission (Pl/Passes.pm) that skips the op -- if so the
fast path needs an overload guard, not a removal, since the overwhelming
majority of sorts are on plain strings and must stay fast (CLAUDE.md design
principle 2: speed wins).  Measure the cost before and after.

RELATED: #964's family (a value that is plausible but not perl's).  Not the
same as the overload dispatch work in flight in s464aw -- this one is located
precisely in sort's default comparator; coordinate before fixing so the two
do not collide in the same runtime function.
=== DONE (s470bk) ===
FIXED, own commit, runtime-only.  `p-sort`'s no-comparator arm routes through
`p-str-cmp` â the SAME function `sort { $a cmp $b }` already reached and the
same one `%p-sort-classic`'s `:str-asc` uses â so the default and the explicit
block cannot grow two answers (rule 11).

SPEED, which the task asked to measure: the overload question is asked ONCE PER
SORT, not per comparison.  `%p-sort-plain-elements-p` is O(n) beside an
O(n log n) sort and its FIRST test is `*p-any-overload-registered*`, a single
memory load that is NIL in every program that never says `use overload` â such
a program keeps the raw `string<` comparator verbatim.  No Kind-A fast emission
had to be removed.

`%p-sort-classic`'s `:default` arm INHERITS it, as its own docstring predicted:
`%p-plain-scalar` answers NIL for a blessed box, so an overloaded element always
reaches `%p-sort-classic-generic`, which is `(apply #'p-sort items)`.

MEASURED: 12 rows one file, byte-identical to perl 5.40.3 â `reverse sort`, a
`cmp` handler given as a METHOD NAME, a class with only `""` (+`fallback => 1`),
the same object twice, a MIXED list, a single element, an undef element, plain
strings, plain numbers, and the handler CALL COUNTS (`cmp=1 str=0` on two
objects; PCL said `cmp=0` before).

NOTE for whoever reads sort.t rows 162-164: they also need `tie %h` (#155), so
they do not go green on this alone â the standalone probe is the acceptance
test, exactly as the task said.  ALSO probed: perl DIES for a class with `""`
and no `cmp` and no `fallback` (`Operation "cmp": no method found`), where PCL
runs on with the string compare â the already-accepted #960(a) divergence, not
a new one.

Gate 203/6831.  Guard `Pl/t/overload-01.t` row 35, inverse-verified.
subject: SILENT WRONG: `sort @objects` (the DEFAULT comparator) ignores an overloaded `cmp` and stringifies through `""` instead -- perl calls cmp once per comparison; the explicit `sort { $a cmp $b }` spelling is correct, so only the default path diverges
